drafted_from: tool row in tools/check-a-rendered-video/tool-rows.json, do-work/check_cut_speech.py and test/test_plan_and_cut_speech.py (CutSpeech), which I ran with the test's tone-word stand-in speech reader
start_here: Say to your AI: "Listen to my cut /work/cut.mp4 against its timeline /work/timeline.json for the ask and reply lines, and show me the first ask, the middle reply and the last reply." It reads the tool's row and runs check_cut_speech.py on your computer.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it reads the plans, recordings and settings file it is given on the person's computer and writes one report file.
instructions: 1. Make the cut with tool:assemble-a-plan-into-a-cut so you have the cut video and its timeline.json (each segment's kind, text, start and length).
2. Choose which spoken kinds to read (for example ask,reply) and which frames to see (kind:first, kind:middle or kind:last).

3. The AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: tool:check-a-cuts-speech-against-its-plan} and runs its `run` command with --cut, --timeline, --work, --kinds and --frames; a speech reader is mlx-whisper on Apple silicon or a command given with --reader.

4. Read the last line {"result": {report, lufs, silences, to_check, frames, listened_by}}: tell the person the loudness, each long silence, each segment to check with the words missing or heard at its ends, and show the frames. When listened_by is null say plainly that nobody has listened to this cut yet; never set it yourself.

worked_examples.title: A reply that runs into the next word
worked_examples.ask: Listen to my cut against its timeline and show me the frames.
worked_examples.given: From tools/check-a-rendered-video/test/test_plan_and_cut_speech.py (test_a_reply_that_runs_into_the_next_word_is_listed_with_the_frames_and_silence), which I ran. The cut is a 320x180 test picture with the eight tone words alpha to hotel; the timeline has an ask "Alpha bravo?" (0.0, 1.3 s), a reply "Charlie, delta echo." (1.3, 1.8 s), a reply "Foxtrot golf." (3.1, 1.8 s) and a card (4.9, 0.5 s). Command: python3 tools/check-a-rendered-video/do-work/check_cut_speech.py --cut /work/cut.mp4 --timeline /work/timeline.json --work /work/one --kinds ask,reply --frames ask:first,reply:middle,reply:last (the test adds --always-show ask and its stand-in reader). It exits 2.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result": {"report": "/work/one/verify.json", "lufs": -15.6, "silences": [1.813208], "to_check": [2], "frames": ["/work/one/frame1.jpg", "/work/one/frame2.jpg", "/work/one/frame3.jpg"], "listened_by": null}} Above it: "cut.mp4 LUFS -15.6 silences over 1 s: [1.813208]", "reply seg 2 100%   HEARD ENDS ['foxtrot', 'golf', 'hotel']" and "listened_by null: nobody has listened to this cut end to end". verify.json also holds each segment's share heard, words missing and what was heard (segment 2: foxtrot golf hotel, end_off true), and frames.jpg lays the frames side by side.
